material_definitions: The electrical properties and the crystal structure were investigated for the ceramic electrolytes based on LiHf2(PO4)3.
The conductivity enhanced by the Li2O addition with LiHf2(PO4)3 system and by the increase of x for Li1+xMxHf2-x(PO4)3 (M = Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu or Y) systems.
The P21/n monoclinic phase transformed to NASICON-type R3c rhombohedral phase at above 1173 K.
The activation energy for bulk component was 0.42 eV for the NASICON-type structure.
The material series studied is LiHf2(PO4)3 + yLi2O (y=0.1).
The sample was sintered at 1298 K, which yielded the maximum total conductivity.
Li2O addition acts as a flux, promoting high densification and the formation of the NASICON-type (R3c) phase.

material_definitions: The ceramic electrolytes are based on LiHf2(PO4)3 systems, specifically Li(1+x)MxHf(2-x)(PO4)3 where M=Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, or Y.
Samples were sintered at temperatures above 1293 K to obtain maximum conductivity and high density pellets.
The materials typically formed the NASICON-type structure (R3c structure), although a small amount of P21/n monoclinic phase sometimes remained as a secondary phase.
The maximum conductivity obtained in this series was 1.7e-4 S/cm for the sample with x=0.2 (M=Fe) at 298 K.
